purpose: Assemble one project SSOT document from typed evidence and interview answers. Do not crawl a live repository.

questions.prompt: What is the stable project id? (e.g. wellmanifest.ssot or subactor.widget)
What is the human-facing project name?
What SemVer should the description document declare?
placement.home: which org HOMEs this repository? (wellmanifest | subactor | semcod). "w ramach wellmanifest" means ADOPT, not HOME.
placement.shape: domain_pack | runtime_service | both. runtime_service must not HOME wellmanifest.
placement.runtimeOwner: who runs the CLI/daemon? Same enum as home. Empty inherits home. wellmanifest does not host product daemons.
placement.adopt: which wellmanifest packs to follow? (comma-separated wellmanifest/<pack> ids). ADOPT is not HOME.
One sentence: what is this project for? This is the field humans get wrong when README and schema disagree.
Who owns semantics? (comma-separated ids, e.g. github:wellmanifest/ssot)
If evidence sources disagree on purpose, which source id wins? (dsl-manifest, intent, interview, or empty if purpose above is the resolution)
How does README relate to this document?
If README or marketing copy may differ from schema purpose, what is the KNOWN_DIVERGENT reason? (empty if identical)
Is a code2llm TOON, map.toon.yaml, or other analyzer artifact listed in the evidence index?
If yes, which analyzer? (code2llm-toon, map-toon-yaml, redup, other, none)
Should analyzer output stay evidence-only until a human confirms it? (almost always yes)
Has a human confirmed analyzer hits are real description debt, not noise?
